notes.title: Galactic Map & World History Generator
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44959897/16fb22aaf670b66ea3604c2cb118ac8895d8bb24.gif"][/img][/p][h3]This update is a big one 🙂[/h3][p]I’ve finally finished the reworked [b]history generator[/b]. It’s now much easier to expand with new types of events, and it already makes the galaxy feel much more alive.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44959897/128a696fe7cbb505d181550f06e7c75f971fa350.png"][/img][/p][p]When you look at the galactic map, you’ll now see entire [b]empires[/b] forming. They build fleets, colonize planets, collect taxes, and fight each other. Exploration fleets can establish new settlements, while military fleets can conquer them. Of course, space isn’t safe — fleets might get lost in the void or destroyed in asteroid belts.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44959897/59e2e7e07ffa02f0f66cc09b619ba9c710d24ce3.gif"][/img][/p][p]Settlements have their own stories too. A bad harvest, a raider attack, or even a reactor explosion can reduce their population — sometimes to the point where people abandon the place entirely.[/p][p]All of this happens in a massive simulation that runs [b]before you start the game[/b], generating about 600 years of galactic history. It takes some serious calculations, and watching the progress bar tick along feels like you’re watching centuries of chaos unfold.[/p][p]The generated data is already being hooked into gameplay. Empires created by the simulation appear on the galactic map. If an empire can’t manage to hold a single sector, it’s marked as a [b]fallen empire[/b]. On planetary maps, you’ll see settlements — and behind each one there’s a small history. If you stumble across ruins, you’ll even be able to find out why that settlement was abandoned.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44959897/6f2c078c17d6267ec02782fd75a28802c318fef3.gif"][/img][/p][p]It’s a big step toward making every game feel like it has a unique backstory — a galaxy shaped by centuries before you even arrive.[/p][p][/p][h3]Next Steps[/h3][p]I’m working on generating [b]settlements, fleets, and space stations[/b] directly from the history data, so they’ll appear in the game world as real, interactable objects. This way, the galaxy you explore will feel even more alive, shaped by centuries of simulated history.[/p]

notes.title: Devlog 2: Landing Zone Selection
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! Here's a small update:

Landing Zone Selection: You can now choose your landing spot on the planet. The game shows which tiles your ship will occupy after landing. Choose wisely — large obstacles might damage your ship, and taking off again could become a real challenge.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44959897/470f5ce66b33707866e99cd5cbf769ad1cba8f4f.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44959897/2a508d43e3b04c2c5e74dd0fd965119b936f3897.png[/img]

Improved Planet Generation: Planet flora and natural features are now generated more consistently. Several bugs related to plant placement and saving have been fixed.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44959897/ce922ddd5246d30a10ba492f3c8b0e250b642a39.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44959897/e41aa476351e16c7d59fe6198f656b2914b35e10.png[/img]
Bug Fixes: A bunch of long-standing bugs have finally been addressed. Nothing too flashy, but the game should feel a bit smoother overall.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44959897/d09509567e137692791be46cf9986a5a57eb7f96.png[/img]
Thanks  and stay tuned!

notes.title: Devlog : Planetary Day-Night Cycle, Atmospheric Color, and Shadows
notes.notes:
[b]Planetary Time and Daylight[/b]
Planets now have their own custom day length, independent from Earth’s 24-hour cycle.

Lighting intensity smoothly follows the local time of day – dawn, noon, dusk, and night are now visually distinct.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44959897/5e7470fd716f287cd6d3e6f280e3862e5da36b34.gif[/img]
[b]Atmospheric Color[/b]
The atmosphere tint changes depending on the planet, affecting the color and mood of the sky and terrain throughout the day.

[b]Shadows[/b]
Shadows of large terrain objects (like trees) now update based on the local sun's position.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44959897/6304a507299af143d626450edb25c213af3309a0.gif[/img]
This creates a more realistic and immersive environment, especially noticeable when time is sped up.

[b]Flashlights[/b]
Astronauts now automatically turn on their flashlights when it’s too dark, and turn them off when ambient light returns.

[b]Terrain Visual Polish[/b]
The surface of the planet has been visually improved for better variation and clarity.
